record.title: Beijing opens a call for scientific data centers to support AI-enabled research
record.summary: Beijing opened a call for proposals to build domain scientific data centers for AI-enabled research. The notice and its construction requirements specify data aggregation and governance, AI-Ready preprocessing and annotation pipelines, multimodal processing, research-trajectory datasets, audited access controls, and connection to the municipal open-science-data platform with API and integrated-compute services. Projects may last up to three years; company applicants must provide matching funds at a minimum 2:1 ratio to municipal science funding. Applications are due October 28, 2026. The call establishes requirements, not awards, operating centers or delivered research-data access.
organizations: Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Beijing’s Municipal Science and Technology Commission and Zhongguancun Science Park Administrative Committee published a call on 15 October 2026 inviting proposals for Beijing scientific data centers serving AI-enabled research.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice says projects may run for up to three years, must connect to the municipal science-data sharing platform, and should provide data-service systems with search, API calls and integrated compute support. It requires company applicants to identify funding sources and provide supporting funds at no less than a 2:1 ratio to municipal science funding.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The official construction requirements specify AI-Ready data-processing pipelines, tools for preprocessing, feature extraction and annotation, multimodal processing and trustworthy evaluation; they also call for traceable and reproducible research-process datasets, tiered data access, and audited security controls. These are project requirements, not demonstrated operating capabilities.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The solicitation and construction requirements do not establish which projects will be selected, final budgets, operational data-center capacity, delivered data access or research outcomes. A sample value in the application template is not an announced grant cap.

evidence_gaps.description: No proposal selections, final budgets, operating data centers, delivered data and compute services, or research outcomes were established in the notice or application materials.

brief.importance_rationale: If selected and implemented, shared scientific-data infrastructure with platform and compute integration could improve AI-enabled research capacity in multiple fields. This is a city-level proposal call; the score reflects potential consequence if delivered, not evidence that centers or outcomes exist.
limitations: This is a government solicitation and a set of construction requirements, not evidence that any proposal has been selected or that a center is operating.
The application form contains sample/placeholding entries; no program grant ceiling or award amount was established.
No actual center count, data volume, user access, compute capacity or research outcome is specified by the inspected materials.

technical.claimed_result: The authorities plan to support domain scientific-data centers with AI-Ready data services and research-process records for model training, evaluation and reproducible research.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official call and construction requirements specify AI-Ready data processing, research-trajectory datasets, access controls, platform integration, APIs and compute services. No center has been shown to be selected or operational.
technical.mechanism: Competitive proposals for projects of up to three years, connecting domain datasets to the Beijing municipal open-science-data platform and providing search, APIs, sandboxes and integrated computing. Construction requirements include tools for data preprocessing, feature extraction and annotation; authorized, traceable research-process records; tiered access; and audited security controls. Company applicants must specify funding and provide at least 2:1 matching support relative to municipal science funding.
technical.regime: Beijing municipal program announced 15 October 2026; proposals close 28 October 2026 at 18:00 China Standard Time. The notice targets selected scientific domains and organizations based in Beijing.
technical.reproducibility: The construction requirements describe traceable data and research-process records as a goal. No proposed center, access service, dataset, model-training use or reproducibility outcome was inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: The call says it implements Beijing’s 2026–2028 AI-for-science plan. It does not quantify current data access or compare expected center capacity with a measured baseline.

brief.title: Beijing opens a call for scientific data centers to support AI-enabled research
brief.why_it_matters: The proposal joins AI-ready scientific datasets with research-process traces, reusable access controls, platform integration and compute services. If funded and implemented, that infrastructure could support reproducible research and model training/evaluation across several scientific fields. The solicitation does not establish awards, actual access or research effects.
